subject: Per-token Accelerator: sliding-slab counter-offer and true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Daniel Moss <daniel.moss@evergreenhealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@evergreenhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-25T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: per-token ladder + pilot accelerator

Monica / Ben —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to capture Evergreen's position so we can get alignment quickly:

- We prefer a per-token marginal ladder (breakpoints) rather than blended tiers — cleaner to reconcile monthly.
- Evergreen can commit to an initial 6-month pilot with a 20M token minimum over the pilot period, then a negotiated ramp.
- Critical ask: a guaranteed peak throughput SLA during daytime business hours (we'll attach expected qps profile).
- We need a simple true-up approach at month-end (no retroactive clawbacks that look like refunds).

Can you send a counter with marginal rates at reasonable breakpoints and an example monthly true-up calc? Also please attach a short doc showing how fallbacks to lower-cost variants would work operationally.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Cloud Integrations
Evergreen Health

[Attachment: evergreen_qps_profile.csv (CSV)]

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Daniel Moss <daniel.moss@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: per-token ladder + pilot accelerator

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front and a plan below:

1) We can support marginal breakpoints with a simple monthly true-up. Example worksheet attached.
2) Pilot structure idea: 6 months, 20M committed tokens, with stepped breakpoints at 0-2M, 2-8M, 8-20M, 20M+. Marginal rates apply only to the tokens in each band.
3) SLA: we can commit to daytime QPS target for the Dedicated pool used in the pilot; I'll include the ops runbook excerpt for fallback behaviors.

I've attached a concise counter-offer PDF plus an Excel that shows the monthly true-up math for the pilot and a blended-vs-marginal comparison so you can see the dollar outcomes.

Next step: if this looks directionally ok, we'd like a procurement sync with your team week of Oct 4 to lock legal redlines.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evergreen_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF)] [Attachment: per-token-slab-math.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Daniel Moss <daniel.moss@evergreenhealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@evergreenhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: per-token ladder + pilot accelerator

Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying points from procurement:

- Breakpoints: we don't want a lower-than-baseline marginal rate at the very top band (no 'deep discounts' after 20M) — instead prefer a modest tilt that rewards velocity without creating a cliff.
- True-up: need a transparent monthly calc that we can reconcile against our internal stats; will share a template.
- Credits vs refunds: we prefer credits applied to next invoice (no cash refunds).

Can Redwood provide a sample invoice flow showing an overage credit applied? Also can you run a scenario where traffic spikes concentrate in month 3 of the pilot (we'll provide projected token curve).

Regards,
Daniel

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Daniel Moss <daniel.moss@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-29T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: per-token ladder + pilot accelerator

Daniel —

Appreciate the guidance. Two quick items from pricing:

- We can implement a tapered marginal ladder (top band receives a modest additional discount but is strictly marginal; that prevents the perverse incentive you noted). Example marginal rates (pilot): 0-2M @ $0.0062, 2-8M @ $0.0049, 8-20M @ $0.0039, 20M+ @ $0.0036.
- True-up mechanics: month-end usage is compared against committed monthly equivalent (20M/6 per month) and credits are issued as invoice credits applied to following month. No retroactive cash refunds.

I attached a one-page invoice flow and a worked example with a month-3 spike (the spreadsheet models the spike you mentioned). If you'd rather a blended rate for ease, we can also provide that number for each month; blended ends up slightly cheaper if your usage concentrates early.

Let us know if you want the monthly blended table included in the formal SOW.

—Ben
Head of GTM Pricing, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-commit-terms-diff.docx (DOCX)]

From: Daniel Moss <daniel.moss@evergreenhealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@evergreenhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-30T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: per-token ladder + pilot accelerator

Ben / Monica —

This is helpful. Procurement has two remaining asks before we schedule legal:

1) Can Redwood add a 'corridor protection' clause so that if Evergreen undershoots the pilot commitment by >30% across the 6 months we get a proportional credit rather than remittance? We want downside protection as we validate integration risk.

2) In the spike scenario in month 3, how do burst credits interact with marginal bands? We want to avoid a month where we get charged top-of-ladder marginal rate for spike tokens when we otherwise would have landed in a higher average.

If you can confirm both in writing we'll route to legal for a short review.

Thanks,
Daniel

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Daniel Moss <daniel.moss@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-02T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: per-token ladder + pilot accelerator

Daniel —

Appreciate the detailed asks, and thanks for flagging the corridor/downside protection and burst handling. Two commitments from our side:

1) Corridor protection: we will include a proportional credit clause if total pilot usage < 70% of committed 20M tokens (credit = pro rata of the shortfall applied to the final month invoice). That fulfills the "no-remittance" ask and keeps reconciliation simple.

2) Burst handling and marginal bands: burst tokens in a single day are evaluated within the monthly tally. Our true-up logic applies marginal bands to the monthly total; however, to avoid a spike penalty we will cap the marginal rate applied to any single day's tokens at the prior month's blended marginal average (effectively smoothing single-day spikes). Practically this means: if spikes push you into a higher band for the month, you still benefit from a daily cap so short spikes aren't priced at top-of-ladder without smoothing.

I attached an updated proposal PDF and a short example invoice that shows the corridor credit and burst smoothing. If that looks good, Monica will schedule a legal sync and we'll prepare a short SOW.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evergreen_proposal_v3.pdf (PDF)]
